main_text.p: riores sefe diffundit:tum quia ferum,quo dilutus eft, ipfius calorem temperat. Idcirco fanguinis illud igneum, & fubtile quod in partibus cordi vicinis vi caloris exhalatur; in locis illis minùs calidis calore mediocri adjutum, exitum & fi non minùs moliatur; partes tamen illæ igneæ ubi fanguinis maffam reliquerunt, loco non quidem frigido, fed longè minùs calido à partibus ferofis, frigidifque quibus involvuntur, retinentur; ibique circa renes, ac partes alias inferiores concrefcunt.

Haud aliter atque vapor ille, qui per meatus corporis evadebat, à proprio igne vectus, ubi in superficiem corporis pervenit, externo frigore comprimente faceffit in fudorem. Ac ferè in eundem modum fuligo generatur, cum ignis qui humidum, ac terreftre fert veluti indumentum, parte fubtiliore evadente, reliquum ab ambiente illo frigore fiftitur ac condensatur.
main_text.head: ARTICULUS IV. Quo hac caufa pluribus aliis natura exemplis illuftratur.
main_text.p: CÆterum etsi hæc caufa minimè eft obfcura; natura ipfa fuis operibus eam reddit illuftriorem, Herbæ enim plurimæ quæ in paludibus, ftagnis, rivis, aquifque frigidiffimis nafcuntur valde calidæ funt. Imo in extremis montium receffibus, qui nive ad æftatem teguntur, herbæ oriuntur calidiffimæ, inter quas funt ferè omnes hellebori fpecies. Cujus rei caufa eadem eft quæ adipis concretionis. Frigus nempe ambiens, ac humidum retinens obftat quominus ab æftu folis, calidum internum diffipetur. page.notes: A small stray mark ("*") stands at the right end of the line "concrefcunt." and another near "obftat"; these look like printer's marks, not reference marks, so they are not transcribed. The first word "riores" is a fragment carried over from the previous page. Print is faded at the right edge, but all lines are legible. The word "fiftitur" and "condensatur" are read from the ligatured long-s forms with reasonable confidence.
